claims.text: Adding approximately 3 at.% Al to a refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
Approximately 3 at.% Al is sufficient to promote a continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
The untreated alloy lacks sufficient oxidation-resistant dopants.
The Al addition will produce a continuous, dense, and adherent alumina layer at the alloy surface.
At high temperature, added Al reacts with oxygen to form thermodynamically stable alumina.
The alumina layer acts as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
Restricting oxygen ingress reduces oxidation kinetics.
The alumina barrier will protect the alloy's bulk microstructure during prolonged exposure.
The Al-doped alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate and lower weight gain per unit area than the untreated alloy.
The Al-doped alloy will retain a protective, continuous alumina scale after exposure.
The untreated alloy exhibits rapid oxidation and oxide-scale spallation at approximately 1100 °C in air for 100 hours.
The proposed oxidation-resistance benefit should persist around 1100 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for approximately 100 hours.
The expected benefit is conditional on the Al addition not compromising the mechanical integrity of the load-bearing matrix.
The optimal Al content and the exact kinetics of alumina formation are not yet established.
The interaction between the Al-induced oxide and the alloy microstructure under mechanical load remains insufficiently characterized.
